fields.description: Hugo RAS is Medtronic's modular robotic-assisted surgery system. The manufacturer describes independently positionable arm carts with an innovative tilt joint and multiple degrees of freedom, an open surgeon console that keeps the surgeon connected to the bedside team, and a central system tower that combines KARL STORZ imaging with the Valleylab FT10 energy platform. The arm carts can be moved and shared across the hospital, and the number of carts can be matched to the procedure. A 3D HD endoscope can be placed on any robotic arm, and nine compatible wristed instruments are listed. Medtronic says the system is available in more than 35 countries after more than four years of use. The reviewed pages publish no numeric price, mass, dimensions, payload, speed or battery endurance, and do not establish independent clinical superiority.

highlights: Surgical system with independently positionable modular arm carts
Open surgeon console supports communication with the bedside team
Touch Surgery ecosystem supports surgical video and performance analytics
Medtronic describes Hugo RAS as a modular robotic-assisted surgery system with independently positionable arm carts, an open surgeon console and a central system tower.
Each arm cart has multiple degrees of freedom and an innovative tilt joint; the manufacturer does not publish an exact arm count or total degrees-of-freedom figure.
The system supports nine compatible wristed instruments and a 3D HD endoscope that can be placed on any robotic arm.
The open console is designed to keep the surgeon connected to the bedside team, with easy-grip controllers for instruments across scales.
Medtronic says Hugo is available in more than 35 countries after more than four years of use; no numeric price, mass, dimensions, payload or independent performance result is published.

fields.description: Starship Robot is Starship Technologies' six-wheeled autonomous sidewalk delivery platform. The manufacturer says the robots operate at Level 4 autonomy with remote human assistance available if needed, carry up to three shopping bags in an insulated interior, and run for 18 hours on a single charge with wireless overnight charging. The sensor suite includes 12 cameras including time-of-flight, radars, ultrasonic sensors and neural networks; six wheels and a bogie system support curb climbing, and winter wheels support snow. Starship reports 3,000+ robots, more than 10 million deliveries, eight countries and 125,000 road and driveway crossings per day, and calls itself the undisputed #1 leader in sidewalk autonomous delivery. These are company figures and claims, not independent audits or a measured market ranking.

body-scope-check.versionScopes: Hugo RAS is one modular surgical system; its arm carts, console, tower, instruments and endoscope are components, not separate robot models. Naïo Oz is one wheeled tool carrier; the more than 35 implements are tools, not robot models. Starship Robot is one six-wheeled delivery platform; the Starship company name and its fleet count are not additional models.
body-scope-check.priceScopes: No reviewed source publishes a numeric Hugo, Oz or Starship Robot price. The catalog non-disclosure labels are retained as non-numeric status text, not quotes.
body-scope-check.weightScopes: No reviewed source publishes robot mass for Hugo, Oz or Starship Robot. The existing Starship 38 kg catalog value is not supported by the reviewed page and is cleared.
body-scope-check.sizeScopes: No reviewed source publishes overall robot dimensions for Hugo, Oz or Starship Robot. The Starship catalog size “small” is a directory class, not a measured envelope.
body-scope-check.payloadScopes: Naïo publishes 60 kg lifting capacity, not a total load guarantee for every implement. Starship publishes up to three shopping bags, not a mass rating. Hugo publishes no numeric payload.
body-scope-check.enduranceScopes: Naïo publishes up to 8 hours of operation and says a full working day with a few hours of recharging; Starship publishes 18 hours on a single charge. Neither is a duty-cycle or all-conditions guarantee. Hugo publishes no battery endurance.
body-scope-check.autonomyScopes: Hugo is a surgeon-controlled teleoperated system with modular carts, not an autonomous robot. Naïo describes GNSS RTK autonomy and “Augmented Autonomy”; Starship describes Level 4 autonomy with remote human assistance. These are manufacturer descriptions, not independent safety certification or measured uptime.
body-scope-check.listingScopes: The roboticsdir and buyandrentrobots listings name products and companies; they do not establish prices, current stock, delivered fleets or independent performance.
